messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate (hosted). Error type: upstream gateway timeouts + 5xx from kv-prefix-cache reads. Current 5xx = 12.4% over last 3m. Affected regions: eu-west1, us-central1. Paging oncall.
oncall-bot: Paging @ashok (oncall), escalation level: P1. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/prefix-cache-5xx
ashok: I'm on it. Looking at metrics now — dashboards show a sharp spike in kv read errors and eviction rate at 12:07 UTC. Suspect cache churn/eviction storm causing backend DB fallthroughs and timeouts.
maria: Confirming. Observed TTL drop and concurrent prefix write thrash. Top error: `kv: prefix shard read timeout` in the cache layer. Also seeing `panic: invalid cache index` sporadically in some hosts.
leo: Logs (sample):
```
2026-03-15T12:07:14Z host=cache-3 shard=3 level=error msg="kv read timeout" prefix_key="org:acme:usr:123" latency_ms=12000
2026-03-15T12:07:16Z host=cache-5 level=warn msg="eviction-rate spike" evictions_per_s=452
2026-03-15T12:07:18Z host=cache-2 level=error msg="invalid index" trace=abcd1234
```
ashok: Quick check: cache hit rate collapsed from 98% -> 46% for some prefixes. Backend DB QPS spiked; gateway 504s increased. Customer impact: `acme-pay` and `stripe-sandbox` show highest error volume.
sarah-ops: CS reports: AcmePay experiencing payment retries. CS flagged priority customers, asking for ETA. @jenn can you pull impact table?
jenn: On it. Quick tally: 9 customer clusters hit, top one (AcmePay) 42% of their requests returning 5xx, estimated ~8% of global user-facing traffic affected in the last 10m. Pushing note to status page.
cs-bot: Status page update queued: "Degraded performance for text generation in EU/US regions; engineering investigating."
ashok: Immediate mitigations I'm proposing:
 - toggle prefix-cache prefetching OFF for high-churn prefixes (`prefetch_policy=off`)
 - enable cache-bypass for read path for prefixes with >3s latency (`kv.read.bypass=true`)
 - apply backpressure config to reduce eviction aggressiveness (`evict.backpressure=0.6`)
I can run the first two as dynamic flags.
maria: If we bypass, we should also enable short-circuit fallback to the smaller but stable in-memory read-through layer to avoid hammering DB.
leo: I'll prep a rollout: apply dynamic flag to `edge-proxy` and `cache-coordinator` in eu-west1 first, then us-central1. Plan: 1) disable prefetch, 2) enable bypass, 3) monitor 5xx.
ashok: Running command to disable prefetch on cache-coordinator (eu-west1):
```
infractl flags set cache-coordinator--prefetch_policy=off --region eu-west1 --dry-run=false
```
ashok: Done. Watching metrics...
leo: I pushed `evict.backpressure` to 0.6 in eu-west1 coordinator via k8s env override on the configmap. Rolling restart scheduled with 30s delay per pod.
ashok: Also executed targeted cache flush for the most corrupted shard (shard=3) to clear invalid indices:
```
kv-tools flush-prefix --shard=3 --prefix-filter "org:acme:*" --force
```
maria: Noted. That should help invalid-index errors but will increase DB load momentarily. We're throttling global clients to limit DB QPS.
ashok: Throttle applied: `rate-limit=150r/s per org` on edge-proxy for affected prefix list.
jenn: Throttle and bypass in place. Initial signal: 5xx dropped from 12.4% -> 4.8% in 3m. AcmePay errors down to 18%.
sarah-ops: Good progress. CS notified; they've acknowledged the update.
leo: We saw one pod restart fail due to crashloop on cache-5 after config change; logs show `index bounds` error. Taking that pod out of LB and will rebuild a fresh instance with latest runtime.
ashok: Taking crashloop pod out with `k8s cordon` and `delete pod`. Spun up new host with patched cache runtime (v2.3.7-hotfix) on eu-west1.
ashok: New host healthy, joining cluster. Eviction rate falling. DB QPS now within acceptable range.
maria: Monitoring: 5xx now 1.9% cluster-wide, latency back to baseline for most prefixes. There's still a small tail for long-running requests (~2%).
cs-bot: Sent customer update: "We have implemented mitigations and error rates are decreasing. We will post full incident report after investigation." 
jenn: Temporary mitigation action items:
 - action: postmortem ticket INC-3421 created (owner: ashok)
 - action: add automated detection for `eviction-rate > 300/s` to alert earlier (owner: leo)
 - action: investigate root cause of index corruption (owner: maria)
ashok: Handing off oncall to @leo for the overnight window. Summary for oncall handoff:
 - Root cause: aggressive eviction + prefix churn -> index corruption/kv-read timeouts
 - Actions taken: disabled prefetch, enabled bypass, applied backpressure, targeted flush of shard=3, cordoned bad pod and rolled patched instance, applied throttles
 - Current state: 5xx 1.9% -> trending down, new instances healthy, DB QPS stabilized
 - Customer impact: ~8% global traffic affected at peak; top customer AcmePay saw 42% 5xx. No data loss reported.
 - Next steps: follow-up postmortem, add early alerting, validate index invariants in staging.
leo: Taking handoff. I'll keep watch for at least 4 hours. If 5xx > 3% or eviction-rate > 200/s I'll escalate back to P1 and page engineering.
ashok: Thanks team. Leaving notes in the incident channel and the runbook. If anything spikes I'll be available on call for the first 30m.
sarah-ops: Updating incident ladder and notifying Sales for impacted customers. :white_check_mark:
jenn: I'll draft the customer-facing timeline for CS review.
leo: Marking this thread for post-incident review. Adding links: runbook, logs snapshot, perf graph. 
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, monitoring for rebound. Next update in 15m or on request.
